12D.5 Whoever handles the carcass of unclean animals is to wash their clothes.
14A.1 Whatever animals that have divided or cloven hoofs and chews its cud you may eat.
14A.2 Fishes that have fins and scales may be eaten (Bass, croppie, flounder, cod, haddock, pike, salmon, sunfish, mackerel, snapper, trout, perch, smelt, tuna, etc.).
14A.4 Insects-locust, bald locust, grasshoppers.
14A.5 If a clean animal dies it is considered unclean until evening.
14B.1 Camel (does not have a divided hoof).
14B.2 Rabbits, hares, and rock hyrax (does not have a divided hoof).
14B.3 Cattle which either do not chew the cud or divide the hoof (horse, donkey, quagga, llama, etc.).
14B.4 Swine or hog (does not chew the cud).
14B.5 Creeping things-weasel, mouse, tortoise, turtle, sand reptile, ferret, chameleon, gecko, frogs, toads, snakes, crocodile, lizard, squirrel, raccoon, mole.
14B.6 All water life that does not have fins and scales are not to be eaten (e.g., shrimp, lobster, snails, clams, shark, shell fish, eels, catfish, scallop, octopus, etc.).

14B.8 Unclean birds-Eagle, buzzard, osprey, vultures, kite, ravens, owl, night hawk, ostrich, hawk, little owl, cormorant, great owl, falcon, swan, pelican, stork, herons, hoopoe, bats (and the eggs of unclean birds).
14B.9 All winged insects that walk on all fours.
14B.10 Whatever crawls upon its belly or is multi-footed among all creeping things that creep on the earth.
14B.11 Whatever goes on its paws, among all kinds of animals that go on all fours, are unclean (e.g., dogs, cats, coyote, bears, foxes, etc.).
14F.4 You shall touch no unclean thing, nor touch the carcass of any unclean beast.
14G.8 Laws concerning contact with dead or unclean things.
14G.10 All things that touch a dead unclean animal must be cleansed with water and allowed to set until evening.
